title: Normalized reconstruction from two successive support conditions
statement: Let $X,Z,S,B,K$ be schemes [def-pc-scheme], $i:Z\hookrightarrow X$ and $e:B\hookrightarrow Z$ closed immersions [def-weil-closed-immersion], and let $k:K\hookrightarrow X$ and $u:S\hookrightarrow Z$ be complementary open immersions [def-weil-open-immersion] with $\operatorname{range}(k)=(\operatorname{range}(i))^c$ and $\operatorname{range}(u)=(\operatorname{range}(e))^c$. Assume $k,u$ are quasi-compact morphisms. Let $R$ be any sheaf of commutative rings on $X_{\mathrm{proet}}$ [def-weil-pbc-proetale-site], and interpret module sheaves through the canonical additive ring-object realization of [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category] with coefficient rings obtained by inverse image of $R$ [def-weil-proetale-inverse-image]. Use the specified module adjunction $i^{-1}\dashv i_*$ [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-topoi-module-adjunction], with unit $\eta_i$ and counit $\varepsilon_i$, and $u_!\dashv u^{-1}$, with unit $\eta_u$ and counit $\varepsilon_u$, where $u_!$ is the sheafified extension-by-zero functor [lem-weil-pbc-proetale-ringed-open-closed]. Let $A$ be an $R$-module sheaf on $X$, $M$ a module sheaf on $S$, and $\sigma:u^{-1}i^{-1}A\xrightarrow{\sim}M$ an isomorphism. Suppose $k^{-1}A=0$ and $e^{-1}i^{-1}A=0$. Then $\lambda=\varepsilon_{u,i^{-1}A}\circ u_!(\sigma^{-1})$ and $\theta=i_*(\lambda^{-1})\circ\eta_{i,A}$ are isomorphisms, and $\theta$ is the unique morphism satisfying $u^{-1}(\varepsilon_{i,u_!M})\circ u^{-1}i^{-1}(\theta)=\eta_{u,M}\circ\sigma$. The maps are natural for commuting pairs $A\to A'$, $M\to M'$ for which $A'$ satisfies the same two vanishing conditions and $\sigma'$ is the corresponding isomorphism.

source.place: Composite consequence of Tag 09AH, lemma-ses-associated-to-open, applied to two successive complementary pairs. The specified adjunction transpose and its normalization are the support-reconstruction argument extracted from the parent, not a verbatim theorem in that tag.

proof.text: Write $F=i^{-1}$, $G=i_*$, $L=u_!$, $H=u^{-1}$ and $N=FA$; thus $\sigma:HN\xrightarrow{\sim}M$. Apply the ringed open–closed theorem to the complementary pair $(i,k)$, over the ring sheaf $R$. Its hypotheses hold because $i$ is closed and $k$ is its quasi-compact open complement. It gives a short exact sequence $0\to k_!k^{-1}A\to A\xrightarrow{\eta'_{A}}GFA\to0$, where $\eta'$ is the unit of the adjunction used in that theorem. The specified adjunction of the statement has the same right adjoint $G$ (with its $R$-action through the ring unit) and a left adjoint isomorphic to $F$ (via $i^{-1}R\otimes_{i^{-1}R}i^{-1}(-)\cong i^{-1}$). By the conjugate-isomorphism unit equation with $\delta=\mathrm{id}_G$, there is a natural isomorphism $c$ with $\eta_{i,A}=G(c_A)\circ\eta'_A$. So $\eta_{i,A}$ is an isomorphism once $\eta'_A$ is. Since $k^{-1}A=0$, its extension by zero is zero (extension by zero is exact). Hence $\eta'_A$, and therefore $\eta_{i,A}$, is an isomorphism. Explicitly, in this abelian module category the short exact sequence now makes $\eta'_A$ a cokernel of $0\to A$; the identity of $A$ is another such cokernel, so uniqueness of cokernels supplies its two-sided inverse.

source.place: Tag 09AH, lemma-ses-associated-to-open, with the arbitrary-ring-sheaf module formulation of lem-weil-pbc-proetale-ringed-open-closed.

proof.text: Apply the same ringed open–closed theorem on $Z$ to $(e,u)$ and the coefficient ring $i^{-1}R$; $u$ is precisely the quasi-compact complement of the closed immersion $e$. It gives $0\to LHN\xrightarrow{\varepsilon_{u,N}}N\to e_*e^{-1}N\to0$. The hypothesis $e^{-1}N=0$ makes the right-hand term zero (closed direct image is exact). Thus $\varepsilon_{u,N}$ is an isomorphism: it is a kernel of $N\to0$, and the identity of $N$ is another such kernel. Functoriality carries the inverse pair $\sigma,\sigma^{-1}$ to an inverse pair under $L$. Consequently $\lambda=\varepsilon_{u,N}\circ L(\sigma^{-1}):LM\to N$ is an isomorphism.

proof.text: The transpose formula for $F\dashv G$ sends $\lambda^{-1}:FA\to LM$ to $\theta=G(\lambda^{-1})\circ\eta_{i,A}$. Steps 1–2 show both factors are isomorphisms, so $\theta$ is an isomorphism. Its inverse transpose is exactly $\lambda^{-1}$: naturality of the closed counit and the left triangle identity give $\varepsilon_{i,LM}\circ F\theta=\lambda^{-1}\circ\varepsilon_{i,FA}\circ F(\eta_{i,A})=\lambda^{-1}$. This uses the specified adjunction, rather than an independently chosen identification of $FG$ with the identity.

proof.text: For $L\dashv H$, naturality of the unit at $\sigma^{-1}:M\to HN$ and the right triangle identity give $H\lambda\circ\eta_{u,M}=H(\varepsilon_{u,N})\circ HL(\sigma^{-1})\circ\eta_{u,M}=H(\varepsilon_{u,N})\circ\eta_{u,HN}\circ\sigma^{-1}=\sigma^{-1}$. Since $H\lambda$ is invertible, this implies $H(\lambda^{-1})=\eta_{u,M}\circ\sigma$. Applying $H$ to the last equation of Step 3 yields the required restriction equation $H(\varepsilon_{i,LM})\circ HF\theta=\eta_{u,M}\circ\sigma$.

source.place: Tag 0037, definition-adjoint and the following paragraph (transpose formulas); lemma-unit-counit-relations (triangle identities).

proof.text: Let $h:A\to GLM$ be any morphism with that restriction, and let $q=\varepsilon_{i,LM}\circ Fh:N\to LM$ be its inverse transpose. The prescribed restriction says $Hq=\eta_{u,M}\circ\sigma$. Naturality of the open counit and the left triangle identity imply $q\circ\lambda=q\circ\varepsilon_{u,N}\circ L(\sigma^{-1})=\varepsilon_{u,LM}\circ L(Hq\circ\sigma^{-1})=\varepsilon_{u,LM}\circ L(\eta_{u,M})=\mathrm{id}_{LM}$. Cancelling the isomorphism $\lambda$ gives $q=\lambda^{-1}$. Injectivity of the closed adjunction Hom bijection gives $h=\theta$. This proves uniqueness among all morphisms.

source.place: Tag 0037, definition-adjoint and the following paragraph (transpose formulas); lemma-unit-counit-relations (triangle identities).

proof.text: Let $a:A\to A'$ and $b:M\to M'$ satisfy $b\circ\sigma=\sigma'\circ HFa$, and put $N'=FA'$. Rearranging gives $HFa\circ\sigma^{-1}=(\sigma')^{-1}\circ b$. Naturality of the open counit gives $Fa\circ\lambda=\varepsilon_{u,N'}\circ L(HFa\circ\sigma^{-1})=\lambda'\circ Lb$. Hence $(\lambda')^{-1}\circ Fa=Lb\circ\lambda^{-1}$. Naturality of the closed unit now computes $GLb\circ\theta=G(Lb\circ\lambda^{-1})\circ\eta_{i,A}=G((\lambda')^{-1})\circ GF(a)\circ\eta_{i,A}=G((\lambda')^{-1})\circ\eta_{i,A'}\circ a=\theta'\circ a$. These are the asserted naturality squares for $\lambda$ and $\theta$.

Assume $k,u$ are quasi-compact morphisms: their inverse images of affine opens are quasi-compact. Let $R$ be any sheaf of commutative rings on $X_{\mathrm{proet}}$ [def-weil-pbc-proetale-site]. All module sheaves [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category] below have coefficient rings obtained by inverse image of $R$ [def-weil-proetale-inverse-image]. Use the specified module adjunction $i^{-1}\dashv i_*$ [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-topoi-module-adjunction], with unit $\eta_i$ and counit $\varepsilon_i$, and $u_!\dashv u^{-1}$, with unit $\eta_u$ and counit $\varepsilon_u$, where $u_!$ is the sheafified extension-by-zero functor [lem-weil-pbc-proetale-ringed-open-closed]. $$\lambda=\varepsilon_{u,i^{-1}A}\circ u_!(\sigma^{-1}):u_!M\longrightarrow i^{-1}A$$
